content_blocks.title: Why this matters
content_blocks.text: An interactive Shiny app connects validated inputs to reactive calculations and outputs; it also needs error states and data-protection boundaries. The example is intentionally small so you can predict its result before checking it in a local R session.

content_blocks.title: Work through it
content_blocks.text: Trace an input through one calculation to an output, then test missing, invalid and slow-operation behavior. Change one input or condition at a time, compare the observed result with your prediction, and write down one limitation.

content_blocks.title: R example: Introduction to Shiny
content_blocks.code:
# Shiny fragment (static, not run in the browser preview)
ui <- shiny::fluidPage(shiny::sliderInput("n", "Sample size", min = 10, max = 100, value = 30))
content_blocks.expected_output: A Shiny UI definition containing a sample-size slider is created in an R environment with Shiny installed.
content_blocks.run_instructions: CodeLeaf does not provide an R runtime. This block is an inspectable reference example; execute it in a local R console or a reviewed R-aware environment. Static validation checks file structure, not R semantics.
content_blocks.reset_steps: No example is executed by this CodeLeaf lesson. For a local run, use synthetic data in a temporary working directory, avoid production credentials or destructive writes, and restart a clean R session to clear lesson objects.
content_blocks.limitations: Shiny apps need an R process and a suitable host; a browser-only HTML preview cannot execute R. Verify the snippet and expected output with the supported R and package versions before publishing.

content_blocks.title: Common pitfall
content_blocks.text: Do not treat a syntactically plausible example as proof of correctness. For introduction to shiny, check the input type, missing/empty cases, output shape, and domain assumptions.

common_mistakes.problem: Assuming inputs are valid because the UI restricts the normal interaction.
common_mistakes.why: Requests, empty states and malformed values can still reach server logic.
common_mistakes.fix: Validate input in server-side code and display clear recoverable errors.

common_mistakes.problem: Putting too much state into one reactive expression.
common_mistakes.why: Hidden dependencies make updates difficult to reason about and test.
common_mistakes.fix: Keep calculations focused and make reactive dependencies explicit.

common_mistakes.problem: Displaying private data without checking who may access it.
common_mistakes.why: A reactive output can expose records if authorization is not checked.
common_mistakes.fix: Apply server-side authorization and test denied-access cases.
